messages.author: 580c1540ff71f5be
messages.subject: CFA ordinal and missing data
parts:
Dear all, 

I am running a CFA on a 4-point 4-item scale (ordinal) accross 12 groups (countries with approx n= 1000 per group), with some missing data (max 9% in an item in one country) and I am considering 3 options. I was wondering which one is "less bad": 

OPTION 1) cfa (specified_model, data = nameofdataset, std.lv = F, meanstructure = T, ordered = TRUE). I read in this forum that this option is more reliable than setting the estimator manually. However, how is best to deal with missing data in this case?

OPTION 2) cfa(specified_model, data = nameofdataset, sampling.weights = "wgt_scaled", std.lv = F, meanstructure = T, estimator = "MLR", missing = "ml"). However, the scale is not really symmetric...

OPTION 3) cfa (specified_model, data = nameofdataset, sampling.weights = "wgt_scaled", std.lv = F, meanstructure = T, estimator = "WLSMV"). However, I cannot assume MCAR (from Little's MCAR Test), and the model runs with estimator = "WLSMV" but not when I add missing = "pairwise". It gives the following warning:
Error in stats::cov.wt(X[[g]], wt = WT[[g]], method = "ML") :
  'x' must contain finite values only (even if I have removed rows with only NAs)

Options 1 and 2 give similar results and option 3 is much more lenient. What would you recommend? 
Thank you in advance.

Ariadna

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: CFA ordinal and missing data
parts: OPTION 1) cfa (specified_model, data = nameofdataset, std.lv = F, meanstructure = T, ordered = TRUE). I read in this forum that this option is more reliable than setting the estimator manually. However, how is best to deal with missing data in this case?

ordered=TRUE just means you want lavaan to treat all observed variables as ordinal, which has nothing to do with missing data.  The default will be DWLS estimation (WLSMV) with listwise deletion, but you can optionally set missing = "pairwise"
OPTION 2) cfa(specified_model, data = nameofdataset, sampling.weights = "wgt_scaled", std.lv = F, meanstructure = T, estimator = "MLR", missing = "ml"). However, the scale is not really symmetric...

Symmetry is not the issue.  There are only 4 possible values, so data cannot really follow a normal distribution.  MLR will adjust for excess kurtosis (the real problem) if you want to pretend your data are continuous, which will not really affect your structural parameters. So this is an option if you want to use FIML and your modeled variables can justify your MAR assumption.

Why does this example (and the next) have sampling weights, yet your first example does not?  Perhaps because lavaan cannot apply sampling weights when using the latent-response assumption (ordered=TRUE), only when data are continuous.
OPTION 3) cfa (specified_model, data = nameofdataset, sampling.weights = "wgt_scaled", std.lv = F, meanstructure = T, estimator = "WLSMV").

I don't see what you think the advantage would be of using DWLS estimation when treating your data as continuous.

Another option is pairwise ML, for which there are additional missing= options listed in the ?lavOptions help page.  Find details here:

https://doi.org/10.1111/bmsp.12243

The paper has lavaan syntax examples in their Supporting Information document linked in the paper.

Terrence D. Jorgensen    (he, him, his)
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
